title: Extreme Polarization of the Optical Gap and High-Energy Exciton Landscape in CrSBr
authors: Sayantan Patra, Sourabh Jain, Bhumika Chauhan, Marie-Christin Heißenbüttel, Abhisek Saidarsan, Ranjuna M. K., Kseniia Mosina, Zdeněk Sofer, Michael Rohlfing, Thorsten Deilmann, Ashish Arora
abstract: We reveal a strongly anisotropic excitonic landscape in monolayer and bulk-like CrSBr using optical absorption spectroscopy and $GW$-Bethe-Salpeter equation $\textit{ab initio}$ calculations. The direct absorptive determination of the lowest bright optical onsets i.e. $X_0^a$ and $X_0^b$ excitons for the two in-plane polarization eigenaxes yield an in-plane optical gap anisotropy of $470 \pm 15$ meV. This is the highest observed value for any material in the near-infrared-to-visible spectral region to the best of our knowledge. Energetically above, we identify multiple strongly polarized excitons spanning $1.25$ eV to $3.1$ eV selectively aligned along the two orthogonal axes. A resonance $X^-$, located $24$ meV below the $X_0^b$ progressively transfers oscillator strength to $X_b^0$, a behavior consistent with a coupled trion (Fermi-polarion)/exciton pair. Our experiments also provide polarization-resolved broadband dielectric functions of CrSBr. These results establish CrSBr as a strongly polarization-selective excitonic system and highlight its potential for polarization-selective optoelectronics enabled with its large optical-gap anisotropy.
summary: This work investigates the optical properties of CrSBr in both monolayer and bulk forms, revealing a large and highly anisotropic optical gap. By combining polarization-resolved spectroscopy with GW-BSE calculations, the authors confirm CrSBr's potential for polarization-selective optoelectronics due to its extreme excitonic anisotropy.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the highly anisotropic excitonic landscape and optical gap in CrSBr, investigating differences between monolayer and bulk-like forms.
main_result: The research establishes CrSBr as a strongly polarization-selective excitonic system, reporting an in-plane optical gap anisotropy of $470 \pm 15$ meV, which is a record value in this spectral region.
method: The study combines polarization-resolved optical absorption/reflectance spectroscopy with advanced *ab initio* GW-Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is CrSBr, examined in both monolayer and bulk-like forms. The analysis focuses on excitonic transitions and the resulting optical anisotropy.
key_observables: Optical gap anisotropy ($\Delta E_{	ext{opt}}$), polarization-resolved exciton resonances, broadband dielectric functions, and optical constants ($	ilde{n}, \epsilon$).
important_parameters: The anisotropy value ($470 \pm 15$ meV), the energy range (1.25 eV to 3.1 eV), and the comparison between monolayer and bulk samples.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to accurately measure polarization-dependent optical constants and the validity of the GW-BSE framework for describing excitons.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate polarization-resolved absorption spectra for both axes, the extracted polarization-dependent optical constants, and comparisons between experimental and theoretical spectral fits.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of presenting experimental measurements (polarization-resolved spectroscopy) to determine key optical parameters, which are then corroborated and explained using advanced theoretical calculations (GW-BSE).
why_interesting: The strong polarization dependence and large optical gap anisotropy make this material highly relevant for designing next-generation polarization-selective optoelectronic devices, connecting solid-state physics to applied quantum optics.
